proves: the five object-fit rules against one 8x4 image in five 72x72 boxes, with a picture whose edges are distinguishable from its middle
checkable: 420x110 on white, five 72x72 cells on #f0f0f0 at x=8, 88, 168, 248 and 328, spanning y=19..90. Exact rectangles: Fill fills the cell, x+0..+71 and y 19..90. Contain is 72x36 centred, x+0..+71 and y 37..72. Cover is 144x72 cropped to the cell, x+0..+71 and y 19..90. None is the picture at its own size, x+32..+39 and y 53..56. ScaleDown is identical to None to the pixel, because the picture is smaller than the box.
the_discriminator: Fill and Cover both fill the cell, so the rectangle cannot tell them apart - what tells them apart is which part of the picture survives. The source has a magenta column at its own x=0 and a cyan column at x=7. Read them at the cell's x+1 and x+70 on row 50: Fill shows 232,40,200 and 40,200,200 because it squeezes the whole picture in; Cover shows neither, because covering a square box with an 8x4 picture crops the outer quarter from each side. Contain shows both. None and ScaleDown show both too, but only within their four rows at y=53..56.
why_the_source_changed: the first version of this fixture used a picture of four solid quadrants, which is symmetric: cropping it horizontally leaves the same left-red right-green picture that stretching it does. Fill and Cover differed by 5,103 pixels of 5,184 and by the column the boundary landed in - 37 against 38 - which reads decisive and is not. Every one of those differences is resampling softness, so a Cover implemented as Fill would have failed this fixture by an interpolation artefact rather than because the crop was wrong. A fit is *where the picture is cut*, so the picture has to have something at its edges to lose. This is the ellipse in a square cell again, one property along.
status: measured from the committed image; the rectangles are also asserted in paint.rs unit tests independently of it. Needs a Chrome number - `object-fit` is exactly expressible on an - and the measurement is worth taking now that the scene can discriminate.
